public_rationale: Contemporary evidence points in different directions. FineMatch documents weaknesses in fine-grained mismatch detection. ConceptMix finds useful agreement between automated checks and human judgments. Neither directly tests the complete self-checking and corrective-feedback task described in the post. These findings do not settle the broad claim that current technology was quite poor at it.
limitations: The evidence concerns related checking tasks, not an exact replication of the claimed workflow.
Results from earlier 2024 models do not fully characterize every system available in December.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current AI technology is quite poor at checking whether its own image output satisfies the prompt and feedback, and new technology may be needed.

statement.excerpt: But current technology has proven quite poor at such sanity checks. New technology may be needed.
statement.document_title: Don’t Ride This Bike! Generative AI’s persistent trouble with compositionality and parts

from_speaker: quite poor at such sanity checks
our_interpretation: Sanity checks means detecting whether a generated image satisfies its prompt and subsequent corrective feedback.
The plain reading concerns practical reliability on the compositional and part-related tasks discussed in the post.
Current refers to technology available by December 8, 2024. Research has no standard quarterly reporting period, so the observation window is the latest reporting year to date.
The suggestion that new technology may be needed expresses a possibility, not a separately resolvable forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Direct evaluations show frequent failures to detect prompt and feedback violations in images generated by contemporary systems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Direct evaluations show reliable detection of those violations across the relevant compositional and part-related tasks.

evidence.locator: Section 1; related experimental findings in sections 4.2 and 5
evidence.explanation: FineMatch finds weaknesses in compositional mismatch analysis by GPT-4V and Gemini Pro Vision, while reporting improvements from task-specific training. Its benchmark does not directly measure a generator checking its own outputs against successive user corrections.

evidence.locator: Introduction, contribution 2; section 3 and appendix A.3
evidence.explanation: ConceptMix reports 0.81 consistency between GPT-4o and human-majority judgments, compared with 0.85 among human evaluators. This challenges a blanket characterization of checking as poor, but uses decomposed concept questions rather than the full self-checking and feedback task.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A human-validated evaluation of December 2024 systems detecting relational, numerical, and part-related violations in their generated images, including violations of corrective feedback.
